contributions.statement: For a codebase Q&A assistant over the Java repos, give developers a tool-using exploration agent (symbol lookup, file reads, optionally semantic search) rather than one-shot top-k embedding RAG: on a 30-question Java subset the agents scored 59-63/100 versus 47-49 for RAG, at roughly 13x the tokens.
contributions.evidence: App. D Table D1: SWE-agent 58.89, OpenHands 59.51 and DeepRepoQA 63.29 vs Function-Chunking RAG 46.61 and Sliding-Window RAG 48.73 on Strata, Fineract and Shiro. Table 2 (Python, 4 backbones): DeepRepoQA leads the better RAG by 3.3-10.7 points, but OpenHands leads it by only 1.2-1.4 on Qwen3-Coder and GPT-5.1. Token cost from Table B1. Caveats: authors' own benchmark and LLM-judge rubric, single run, the Java backbone is not stated, single-repo questions only.
relative_to: 2608.01507: on the same SWE-QA set a vector-search ReAct agent beat a grep-plus-subagent agent
2605.29277: tool agent vs closed-book on repository QA
known practice: agentic grep/read exploration rather than code RAG in production harnesses (2609.00006)

contributions.statement: Make the codebase-QA agent re-read the cited span right before answering and, for 'where is X' questions, check that the question's literal identifier appears in the cited file:line span; the main wrong-location failure ended on a similarly named function in another file.
contributions.evidence: App. E.3 (all answers scoring >=73 reached the correct file within two hops; 80% used FindClass or FindFunction with a file_pattern; ViewCode before Finish correlated with Correctness) and App. E.5 (parse_args_spec answered with _extract_func_kwargs_as_ast_nodes, Correctness 2/20). Caveats: manual inspection of selected trajectories, no denominators, correlational.
relative_to: 2606.24834: require file:line citations that a deterministic check confirms
2606.30689: grep-checkable citation IDs catch hallucinated references

contributions.statement: Cap a repository-QA exploration agent at about 10-20 expansion steps: going from 5 to 10 nodes added 7.9 points, 10 to 20 added 2.4, and 30 nodes scored the same as 20.
contributions.evidence: §5.3 Table 4 (55.06, 62.97, 64.43, 65.33, 65.15 at 5/10/15/20/30 nodes). Caveats: Qwen3-Coder only, one run per budget, MCTS nodes are not the same as ReAct turns, LLM-judged.
relative_to: diminishing returns from larger agent step budgets (known; P24)

reason: The MCTS machinery itself does not survive: its margin over a plain ReAct agent is within judge error, and Cursor still scores higher. What survives is a moderate, cross-backbone and Java-checked gap in favour of exploration agents over one-shot embedding RAG for repository questions. The other two items, the symbol-anchoring and literal-identifier checks and the step budget, are weaker and remain hypotheses.
